headlines.title: China seen doing ‘just enough’ with targeted fiscal support to defend GDP growth
headlines.summary:
China’s finance minister has pledged to roll out incremental and targeted fiscal policies to help achieve leadership’s full-year growth target for the country, following a freshly announced package of supportive measures. However, analysts expect Beijing to stop short of a major stimulus, providing only “just enough” support to meet the target.

headlines.title_en: MOFCOM spokesperson answers reporters' questions on the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting and related matters
headlines.summary_en: Q: From September 30 to October 1, the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting was held in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA. It is understood that the meeting reached a joint statement on opposing the weaponization of food, but did not form an outcome document on addressing overcapacity, eliminating forced labor, or adjusting the most-favored-nation principle. How does China evaluate this meeting? What role did China play? A: At this G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting, members exchanged views on topics set by the U.S. presidency, including opposing the weaponization of food, addressing overcapacity, eliminating forced labor, and adjusting the most-favored-nation principle, and reached a joint statement on the food issue, while no outcome document was formed on the other topics. headlines.title_en: HKEX chief executive: International investors are turning their attention to the Chinese market; HKEX will launch RMB-denominated gold futures
headlines.summary_en: [HKEX Chief Executive: International investors are turning their attention to the Chinese market; HKEX will launch RMB-denominated gold futures] Hong Kong's 2026 Policy Address proposed deepening Hong Kong's global offshore RMB business and capital market. HKEX Chief Executive Chan Yiting said on the 2nd that international investors have refocused their attention on Asia, especially the Chinese market, and are interested in diversified asset allocation. Hong Kong needs to build a diversified asset ecosystem, rather than only expanding and strengthening the stock market. HKEX will study launching RMB-denominated gold futures.

headlines.title_en: A-shares: New stocks had zero first-day declines in the first three quarters; 4 major winners each posted over 300,000 yuan in paper gains; 19 stocks rose more than 500% on their first day
headlines.summary_en: According to The Paper, in the first three quarters of 2026, A-share IPOs had zero first-day breakages, and more than 40% of first-day closing per-lot floating profits exceeded 10,000 yuan. According to Wind data, in the first three quarters of this year, 123 companies listed on the A-share market, and none had broken issue price by the first-day close. At the same time, 57 new shares in the A-share market had per-lot floating profits of more than 10,000 yuan (Shanghai and Shenzhen new shares are 500 shares per lot, Beijing Stock Exchange new shares are 100 shares per lot) (calculated based on the first-day closing price, the same below), accounting for 46%. In terms of first-day closing floating profits, among the new shares listed in the first three quarters, 10 new shares had first-day closing per-lot floating profits exceeding 100,000 yuan, of which 7 were STAR Market-listed companies, including 4 super "big meat" lots with per-lot floating profits exceeding 300,000 yuan. In terms of first-day gains, among the 123 new shares, 19 rose more than 500% on the first day, and 96 new shares doubled by the first-day close, accounting for 78%.

headlines.title_en: The IPO market continued to recover in the first three quarters; equity financing exceeded 750 billion yuan; IPO fundraising rose 180% year on year; no newly listed stock broke issue price
headlines.summary_en: According to Shenzhen Economic Daily, in the first three quarters of this year, the A-share IPO market continued to recover, with fundraising scale rising sharply. According to Wind data, in the first three quarters of this year, A-share equity financing reached 750.861 billion yuan, of which 123 companies raised 216.315 billion yuan through IPOs, up 180% year on year; 175 companies raised 465.489 billion yuan through additional issuance, down 40% year on year; 60 companies raised 68.572 billion yuan through convertible bonds, up 56% year on year; 1 company raised 484 million yuan through rights issue. According to Wind data, in the first three quarters of this year, there were 123 A-share IPO companies, with total IPO fundraising of 216.315 billion yuan.
